title: Your Agents Need Discipline
transcript: Did you know that there's a problem with AI coding agents? Although they're useful to write code, software development is not just writing codes. You need a scope, test, review, documentation, and at the end someone needs to decide if the pull request is safe to merge or not. But most of the time, we give one AI agent to do all this job at the same time. So essentially it becomes product manager, developer, tester, reviewer, and release manager at the same time. And then we wonder why it's randomly changes some files, it skip test, or forget the instructions, and says done without telling you what has been done. And that's exactly reason why we built agent crew. Agent crew is a markdown first process layer for AI coding agents. It gives the agents roles, skills, routing, project memory, which is really important, and hands-offs. So it's designed to go for two process, >> [music] >> full lane and fast lane. For example, a typo, you don't need all your agents to work on it to fix a typo in your code. You just need a developer just to fix it fast. But the problem like authentication, you need full lane. You need security reviewer, you need project manager for the scope, you need a reviewer and tester to test it because it's a sensitive functionality. And agent crew does that for you automatically. And that's important because the same model that writes you code, [music] with agent crew it will not be the only reviewer of that the same code. So the point of all of this is that please don't blind trust on what agents are writing for you. You need to define a discipline for your agents because powerful tools need process. I add a link to the description. You can watch the full video about agent crew. And you can check the agent crew in the GitHub. It's open source, you can use it for free.
